judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence stating that all requisite resolutions have been adopted; nothing elastic in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.B.3 and is consistent with X.C's survival rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "to ENET's best knowledge" and "does not know of any valid basis" are knowledge qualifiers of familiar type; the repetition of the no-pending-proceedings sentence is redundant rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels X.B.4, except that the University's version adds an adverse-impact qualifier this one lacks — an asymmetry, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "EENET" is a typographical slip and "has reasonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a notably vague financial representation whose content a court would have to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines or supports this assurance, and Section XI gives the University no financial-condition termination right to give it teeth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite organisation and eligibility representation, restated as a continuing covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise to retain eligibility to hold the License sits against VIII.B, which lets the University surrender or not renew that License — a tension worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Qualified "in all material respects", with conventional no-conflict and no-consent language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against XIII.Q, which acknowledges pre-existing obligations to Hybrid that could conflict with performance here — the very thing the no-conflict representation denies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence about corporate authorisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.A.3 and raises no cross-provision issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge qualifiers and the added "which would have an adverse impact on the University's obligations" narrow the representation, but the wording is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with X.A.4's mirror and with X.C's survival and notification duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about a schedule that, as executed, contains entries marked "Omitted" and incomplete coordinates — the warranty is difficult to apply to that document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.B directs antenna reorientation at receive sites "listed on Schedule A", contradicting this provision's premise that Schedule B is the receive-site list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any event or circumstance which might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is a loose trigger for the notification duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It converts representations into continuing covenants, which interacts with the termination rights in XI.A(2) and XI.B(2) for breach of "material obligations" but does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "breaches any of its material obligations" is undefined, and the "either (a) ... or (b)" structure appears to let the University terminate whenever either limb is met even though (b) is the more forgiving cure standard — a drafting slip that changes the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "without further liability to ENET" is hard to reconcile with XI.C, which preserves the terminating party's damages claim, and termination under this paragraph triggers the $1.00 equipment purchase in III.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1)'s carve-out ("unless such termination is due to a breach by ENET") lets ENET terminate on an event it may have caused, limb (3) lets ENET terminate simply by ceasing to serve the market, and "material obligations" is again undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.A denies the University the $1.00 (and even the market-value) purchase right where ENET exercises "its rights under Section XI.B.(2)", a cross-reference that does not match this paragraph's structure cleanly, and XI.C cuts against "without further liability".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is short and clear in preserving damages claims for the terminating party only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XI.A and XI.B each say termination is "without further liability" to the other party, and II.D, II.E likewise; reconciling those with a preserved damages claim is a genuine internal problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The qualifier "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld" is buried mid-sentence so that its object is unclear, and the closing sentence gives the University an apparently unqualified consent right "[n]otwithstanding anything herein to the contrary".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That absolute consent right is difficult to square with II.A.2 (University must file within thirty days or negotiate), II.C.1 (University shall amend on ENET's request) and III.E.3, all of which assume filings the University cannot simply refuse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mixes "best reasonable efforts" and "reasonable best efforts" within a few lines and requires "such reasonable protests" as ENET requests, standards whose content is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to obtain and maintain all licenses overlaps VIII.A and sits against VIII.B's right to surrender the License; the reimbursement proviso overlaps XII.C and XIII.N.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence repeats "incurred by the University" and is otherwise a plain reimbursement covenant limited to Section XII obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside II.F and XIII.N, the latter beginning "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" and capping certain legal and engineering fees at $15,000 — three overlapping cost-allocation clauses with different scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first permits assignment only if the assignee assumes all obligations, then, "[s]ubject to the foregoing provisions", permits assignment to an entity that does not assume them — an internal contradiction in consecutive sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reproduces VIII.B's assignment machinery with different triggers and, unlike II.B's parallel fee provision, says ENET "shall" (not "may") notify the University about $15,000 in fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts language with a plain effectiveness rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement bears on execution formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "It is the intention of the University" is precatory while "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" is an obligation without any measure of the assistance owed — a genuine open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The distance-learning use must fit within "University Capacity" as defined in Section IV and within the recapture windows there, which this clause never addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional merger and written-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals and XIII.Q preserve the earlier Hybrid Agreement, which is with a different party, so the supersession language does not obviously bite on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of executory character with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not cut against any other provision, though its practical function (bankruptcy characterisation) is not developed anywhere else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated events end in "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" — a catch-all against specifics inviting ejusdem generis — and "the period of dependency of any such contingency" appears to be an error for pendency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "[N]or shall any charges or payments be made in respect thereof" is hard to reconcile with the $2,500 monthly minimum royalty in V.B and the proration rule in V.F.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "best efforts" plus a sweeping negative covenant not to "take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted" is broad and boundary-less.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That negative covenant is difficult to square with VIII.B and XIII.A, which expressly permit the University to surrender, not renew or assign the License in ways that plainly affect ENET's rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Naming a federal statute, agency rules and District of Columbia law as the governing body of law without a priority rule leaves a small ordering question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with XIII.K's forum provision and XIII.P's reformation clause without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings-for-convenience language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It neutralises the several garbled headings in this document rather than creating any conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause disclaims contra proferentem in clear terms; it is itself definite, though it is precisely the tool a court might otherwise reach for in this heavily one-sided instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies across the Agreement and does not conflict with XIII.T's word-meaning rules or XIII.H's governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "District of Columbia courts" is genuinely ambiguous as between the federal courts sitting in the District and the local D.C. courts, and "any party shall have the right to sue" leaves the clause permissive rather than exclusive despite the irrevocable submission that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates the notice provision in XIII.L for service of process, which is consistent, and no other clause addresses forum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed receipt "the first weekday (excluding Federal holidays) after being sent" is definite, and the permitted delivery methods are enumerated exclusively.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception for Royalty payments matches V.C's first-class mail rule, so the two fit; the exclusivity of Express Mail/Federal Express could matter for the many notice deadlines in Sections I, II and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall have the exclusive tight to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" states the option and its exercise mechanics, but says nothing about what happens if ENET does not exercise within twenty-one days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.Q subordinates all ENET rights to Hybrid's D2 rights "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary", and Section IV defines ENET Capacity as D3 and D4 with everything else deemed University Capacity — both pull against this option.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause opens "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein" and then caps only the negotiation fees at $15,000 while leaving "otherwise complying with the terms of this Agreement" uncapped — a general-versus-specific tension in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges ENET to reimburse the University for "operating and maintaining the D Group Station", though III.D makes ENET itself responsible for those costs, and it caps fees that II.F says ENET bears in full.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]either party shall present itself as ... having any relationship with one another, except as set forth under the terms of this Agreement" is oddly absolute and its boundary is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with XIII.C's program-guide listing obligation and Section VII's programming controls, which necessarily involve some public association.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to "promptly negotiate in good faith to reform and amend" with no fallback is a classic open term, and the covenant not to "take any action that contributes to" an adverse regulatory change is very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against XIII.D's written-modification requirement and XIII.P.2's acknowledgement that FCC rules may change the capacity allocation, without saying what happens if negotiation fails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement with no operative obligation; it is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites the same FCC Report and Order as Section IV but dates it July 9, 1994 where Section IV says July 6, 1994, and it subjects the capacity allocation to future rule changes that Section IV states shall not be affected by digital implementation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he obligation of the University to take any action required hereunder shall be read to conform to such other obligations" is an open-ended override, and the proviso barring any action adverse to Hybrid "in the reasonable judgment of the University" gives one party the judgment call.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides everything to the contrary, which directly limits ENET's D2 option in XIII.M and the capacity grant in Section IV, and cuts across the University's affirmative duties in II.C.1, III.E and XII.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, absolute time-of-the-essence rule; clear in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read across the whole instrument it collides with the many soft timing standards — "as soon as reasonably possible" in III.A, "best efforts", "promptly" — and with the automatic extension of all time limits in the force majeure clause XIII.F.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional non-waiver language, though "any other failure in the future or in the past" is awkwardly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the cure-and-notice mechanics in XI.A and XI.B without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "Final Order" definition is carefully drawn in two limbs; "[a]ll pronouns and any variations therefore" contains a small spelling slip that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition is cross-referenced correctly from II.D.1 and is used consistently throughout Sections II, VIII and XIII.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Schedule describes only "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit" and cross-refers to "Subparagraph 3 (C)", a provision that does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as the definitive list of "programming networks identified on Schedule A" that ENET may transmit without consent, while III.B refers to receive sites "listed on Schedule A" — three inconsistent uses of the same schedule.
